summary: Port reproduces the pattern's look almost exactly — same rainbow-ringed radial pulse blobs, byte-for-byte equivalent hue-vs-brightness mapping, same spatial scale, same sweep speed/direction, same 3D behaviour — but its three driving temporal oscillators run at different periods than the original's, so pulses arrive ~12% more often and the original's exact 118.0 s super-cycle is absent.
observations: Rig from the manifest is grid 16x16 (256 px), NOT the cloud — the cloud rig was used only as an extra 3D lens.
Neither side exposes any settable control (probe.json: 'no settable controls' on both). Control surfaces match: both empty.

Both sides compile and run clean over every window tried (6 s to 600 s); no compile or runtime errors, no black-out, no freeze, no decay. Steady state at t=500-530 s (--label late, 20 fps-equivalent): orig meanBrightness avg 32.9, port 35.4, both 'volatile', both still pulsing.

Shared visual language: a large soft radial blob whose value maps to a full rainbow ramp — going outward from the bright core the hue runs magenta -> blue -> cyan -> green -> yellow -> red -> black. Confirmed on both sides in the phase-matched filmstrips (orig --skip 22.2, port --skip 23.2): rings converge inward onto a saturated magenta core over ~0.6 s.

COLOUR MAPPING IS AN EXACT MATCH. Bucketing every lit pixel of 24 dumped frames by 8-bit value and taking the median hue gives identical curves: value 0-15 -> h 0.41/0.42, 32-47 -> 0.68/0.68, 64-79 -> 0.82/0.82, 96-111 -> 0.93/0.93, 128-143 -> 0.02/0.03, 160-175 -> 0.10/0.09, 192-207 -> 0.17/0.16, 224-239 -> 0.22/0.22 (orig/port). Hue is a pure function of value on both sides, and it is the SAME function.
Long-run colour balance identical: over 600 s (2400 frames) orig meanR/G/B avg = 30.6 / 31.8 / 33.4, port = 30.3 / 31.7 / 33.2. Peak whole-rig brightness 141 (orig) vs 137 (port).
Brightness DISTRIBUTION over 600 s is nearly indistinguishable: fraction of frames with meanBrightness <10 = 45.3% orig vs 47.4% port; >60 = 22.3% vs 22.0%; >5 = 64.5% vs 61.9%.

MOTION MATCHES. Block-matched displacement between dumps 0.2 s apart over a 40 s window (201 dumps, +/-10 px search, no pinning at the bound): orig mean (dx,dy) = (3.03, 1.10) px per 0.2 s, port (3.05, 0.80). Median |d| 2.24 vs 3.00 px/0.2 s, mean 3.34 vs 3.47. Both sweep right-and-slightly-down at ~15 px/s on the 16-px grid.

SPATIAL SCALE MATCHES. Mean |luminance delta| between adjacent lit, non-saturated pixels over the same 40 s: orig 12.90 horizontal / 13.35 vertical, port 13.73 / 13.72 — ring wavelength and falloff width agree within ~6%.

BOTH SIDES ARE FPS-INVARIANT (time-based, not frame-stepped). Event start times over 60 s are identical to +/-0.2 s at 5, 10 and 40 fps on each side independently (e.g. orig 0.0, 1.6, 9.3, 14.8, 22.3, 28.6, 31.2, 36.1, 38.4, 44.4, 51.5, 54.3 at all three rates).

BOTH SIDES ARE SEED-INDEPENDENT: meanBrightness series for seeds 1, 7 and 1234 are byte-identical on both sides. Nothing here is stochastic — every timing difference below is a deterministic constant difference, not RNG divergence.

CADENCE DIVERGENCE: over 600 s the original fires 112 pulse events (11.2/min), the port 125 (12.5/min) — the port is ~12% faster. Median peak-to-peak gap 5.50 s on both, but mean gap 5.33 s (orig) vs 4.78 s (port); orig gap range 1.50-7.75 s, port 1.75-7.00 s. Event durations (frames above meanBrightness 20) median 2.2 s orig vs 2.0 s port.

DRIVER-FREQUENCY DIVERGENCE (the root of the cadence gap). Hann-windowed DFT of the 600 s meanBrightness series with parabolic peak interpolation gives three dominant periods per side plus their sum/difference sidebands. ORIGINAL: 5.895 s (0.1696 Hz), 7.373 s (0.1356 Hz), 10.721 s (0.0933 Hz); sidebands at 3.277 s (sum of the first two) and 29.61 s (their difference) confirm those are fundamentals. PORT: 5.763 s (0.1735 Hz), 6.614 s (0.1512 Hz), 20.14 s (0.0497 Hz); sidebands at 3.079 s (sum) and 44.57 s (difference). So oscillator A is ~2% fast, oscillator B is ~10% fast, and oscillator C is ~1.9x SLOW on the port.

SUPER-CYCLE DIVERGENCE: the original repeats EXACTLY. Autocorrelation of its 600 s brightness series peaks at lag 118.00 s with r=0.995, and again at 236.00 s (r=0.983) and 353.75 s (r=0.994) — its three periods are commensurate (118/20 = 5.90 s, 118/16 = 7.375 s, 118/11 = 10.727 s). The port has no such clean repeat: its best long lags are 265.00 s (r=0.971), 40.00 s (r=0.937), 224.75 s (r=0.928), with no harmonic ladder.

3D BEHAVIOUR PRESENT ON BOTH. On the cloud rig (10x10x10, --pixels 1000) both waterfalls show the same comma-shaped rainbow lattice texture with the same index spacing, and flat-sequence neighbour diffs at strides 1, 10 and 100 are all non-zero on both sides in every dumped frame — the field genuinely varies along all three axes on both.

RESOLUTION-INDEPENDENT ON BOTH: re-rendered at grid 8x8 and 48x48, both sides draw the same logical picture (one blob spanning most of the canvas, same ring proportions), just coarser/finer. Whole-window stats are unchanged across grid sizes on both sides (orig mean 31 / motion 23; port mean 33 / motion 25 at both 64 px and 2304 px).

Short-window stats look misleadingly different and should not be trusted here: the 6 s baseline showed orig meanBrightness max 75 vs port 125, and meanG max 100 vs 217 — that is pure phase (the port happened to peak inside the window). The 600 s numbers show no brightness gap at all.
feedback: The look is already right — colour mapping, ring geometry, blob size, sweep speed and direction, 3D falloff and resolution behaviour all match within measurement noise. Do NOT touch the palette or the value->hue mapping; the hue-vs-brightness curve is bucket-for-bucket identical to the original's.

The only real gap is the set of time constants driving the pulse centre. The original's whole-rig brightness envelope is driven by three commensurate periods: 5.900 s, 7.375 s and 10.727 s (exactly 118/20, 118/16, 118/11 — hence its exact 118.00 s repeat, autocorr r=0.995). The port's measure 5.763 s, 6.614 s and 20.14 s. Retune so the three periods land on 5.90 / 7.375 / 10.73 s; the third one is the worst offender at nearly 2x too slow, the middle one is ~10% too fast, the first is within 2%.

Verification target after retuning: (a) event rate over a 600 s window should drop from 12.5/min to 11.2/min; (b) autocorrelation of the meanBrightness series should show a single sharp peak at lag 118.0 s with r>0.99 and harmonics at 236 s and 354 s; (c) the DFT sideband pair should move from 3.079 s / 44.57 s to 3.277 s / 29.61 s.
Nothing else needs changing: no controls exist on either side (correct), both sides are time-based and fps-invariant (correct), both ignore the seed (correct), and neither dies or drifts over 600 s.
